system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar competition, AI acceleration, and conflict-driven economic shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where great-power competition (notably US–China) and a rapid technological arms race in AI interact with regional wars, energy chokepoints and strained financial markets. Feedbacks between security dynamics, technology governance, and commodity/credit shocks are producing systemic volatility and forcing ad hoc diplomatic and market responses, while alliances and institutions are being reworked under pressure.
system_description.scope: States and coalition actors; major non-state belligerents (e.g., Houthis, militias); global markets (energy, debt, equities); multinational tech and defence firms; critical supply chains (rare earths, shipping, datacentres); international institutions and norms (UN, NATO, trade rules); information ecosystems and AI governance processes.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-political-economic-technological system (the global human system embedding politics, markets, ecosystems and infrastructure).
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security clusters (Middle East conflicts, Russo‑Ukrainian war, Korean peninsula)
Global technology and AI ecosystem (platforms, compute, safety governance)
International financial architecture (sovereign debt markets, central banks, capital flows)
Energy and commodities supply chains (oil, diesel, shipping, rare earths)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with Western backers, where combat, long-range strikes and campaign tactics are expanding in scope and reshaping military and economic support patterns.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran, its Houthi proxies, Saudi Arabia and the United States, where proxy missile and drone operations and reciprocal pressure are intensifying and altering regional security calculations.

variables.name: U.S.–China trade and technology competition
variables.description: The United States and China contest tariffs, market access, critical minerals and industrial policy, with export controls, summit diplomacy and supply-chain moves shifting economic interdependence.

variables.name: Global energy supply and refining strain
variables.description: Worldwide oil, diesel and refining and shipping systems, where refinery outages, tanker shortages and rerouted flows are tightening markets and amplifying price and logistical volatility.

variables.name: AI governance and militarization race
variables.description: States, major tech firms and armed forces globally are racing to deploy advanced AI while negotiating safety rules and norms, shifting regulatory regimes and military doctrines.
